newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Financial expert urges Morocco to pursue reforms.
newsitem.headline: Financial expert urges Morocco to pursue reforms.

text.p: Morocco, to meet the target of sustained growth of six percent of GDP, needs to pursue its economic liberalisation, speed up privatisation and improve domestic saving, the head of the U.S.-based Institute of International Finance Inc (IIF) said on Thursday.

"I applaud the progress made by Morocco to reform and open its economy in recent years compared with other countries in the Arab and Islamic world...But many challenges remain," Charles Dallara, IFF managing director, told a news conference.
Dallara, who is on his first visit to the country, said to develop a competitive economy, the Moroccan authorities should continue the reforms programme launched in the early 1980s.
"I am encouraged that despite agricultural problems, the Moroccan government launched financial reform and continued the privatisation of state enterprises," Dallara said.
Morocco suffers from cyclical drought which in 1995 pulled down GDP growth to minus 7.6 percent.

"To meet the target of an annual six percent growth in GDP, excluding agricultural output, Morocco should continue its privatisation programme, reform the bourse, set up a bond market and improve its domestic saving," he said.

Morocco in 1993 launched a privatisation programme to sell state stakes in 114 companies including two oil refineries and several banks by end 1998. It also underwent a stock market reform aimed at more transparency.
Dallara said the IIF planned to start talks with Moroccan private banks in order to "put the Moroccan flag among other flags of country members in the institute."
With 185 members, the IFF's primary goal is to support members' risk management, asset allocation and business development in emerging markets, Dallara added.
Founded in 1983, the IFF is a non-profit worldwide association of financial institutions including commercial banks.
